description.narrative:
Olof Palme International Center (OPC) har inkommit med en ansökan till Sida om finansiering av 6,2 miljoner SEK för att genomföra "Medborgarnas deltagande för ansvarsfullt och öppet styre mot social rättvisa i Nord Makedonien" under perioden januari 2020 - december 2021.
Insatsen syftar till att stärka det civila samhällets organisationers kapacitet och legitimitet och stödja aktiviteter som säkerställer deltagande i politiska, sociala och ekonomiska processer och ansvarsutkrävande av ansvarstagare. Organisationer i det civila samhället kommer att mobilisera medborgarna och öka deltagandet i beslutsprocesser, förbättra öppenheten och ansvarsutkrävande, samt säkerställa respekten för socioekonomiska rättigheter.
Förväntade resultat av insatsen: 1. Programmet avser att se partnerorganisationer stärka deras legitimitet, bygga allianser för gemensamma åtgärder för att påverka politiska dagordningar och ha kapacitet att övervaka genomförandet av politiska beslut. 2. Programmet har för avsikt att se stärkta medborgare och civilsamhällets organisationer som är organiserade, aktivt deltar i och påverkar beslutsprocesser, kräver öppenhet och ansvarutkrävande av ansvarstagare. 3. Programmet har för avsikt att se arsvarstagare följa bestämmelser som rör transparens och ansvarsutkrävande, samarbeta med relevanta delar av det civila samhället och inkludera dem i beslutsprocesser.
OPCs samarbete bygger på stöd till enskilda projekt såväl som till nätverk och allianser som samlas kring gemensamma frågor/komponenter i programmet.

Olof Palme International Center (OPC) has applied to Sida for funding of 6,2 million SEK to carry out the "Citizens´ participation for accountable and transparent governance towards social justice in North Macedonia" during the period January 2020 - December 2021.
The intervention aims to strengthen the capacity and legitimacy of civil society organisations and support activities that ensure the participatory nature of political, social and economic processes and the accountability of duty bearers. Civil society organisations will mobilize citizens and increase participation in decision-making processes, improve transparency and accountability and ensure respect for socio-economic rights.
Expected outcomes of the intervention: 1. The programme intends to see partner organisations strengthen their legitimacy, build alliances for joint actions to influence policy agendas and have capacities to monitor the implementation of political decisions. 2. The programme intends to see empowered citizens and civil society organisations be organised and actively participate and influence decision-making processes, demanding transparency and accountability of duty bearers. 3. The programme intends to see duty-bearers abide to regulations related to transparency and accountability, cooperate with relevant parts of civil society and include them in decision-making processes.
OPC´s cooperation builds on support to individual Projects as well as to networks and Alliances gathered around common issues/components of the program.
The direct target group is programme partner organisations. The indirect target groups, reached by the programme partners, are citizens/organized citizen groups and duty bearers.

The overall objective of the intervention and the project objective, as described in the programme document and assessed in the initial appraisal, have not changed. OPC base their work in the region on their International strategy which is valid 2020-2025.

The programme intended to see empowered citizens and civil society organisations be organised and actively participate and influence decision-making processes, demanding transparency and accountability of duty bearers. 3. The programme intended to see duty-bearers (state institutions) abide to regulations related to transparency and accountability, cooperate with relevant parts of civil society and include them in decision-making processes.

However when it comes to the expected objectives/outcome challenges, OPC mentions that they consider most of their partners now are mature and internally consolidated organisations, and the focus of the work in the next phase is therefore on expected outcomes 2 and 3.

Below is an overview of results achieved by OPC between the period 2020 to 2022:
From 2020 to 2022, OPC continued to strengthen the capacity and legitimacy of civil society organisations and supported activities that ensure the participatory nature of political and social processes and the accountability of state institutions as part of the democratic consolidation in North Macedonia.
During the 2020 to 2022 period, OPC has partnered with five partner organizations in order to accomplish the programme objectives: 1. Glasen Tekstilec (GT) ; 2. Trade Union of Industry, Energy and Mining (SIER); 3. Foundation for Debate and Education IDEA; 4. NGO Info-Centar and 5. Youth Cultural Center, Bitola (MKC Bitola)
The programme has been effective in strengthening the legitimacy of the partner organizations, as well as it has been effective in the alliance-building of partners for influencing and monitoring policy agendas.
1. Glasen Tekstilec (GT) - focused on increasing awareness among workers in the textile, leather, and shoe industries and advocate for workers rights in the sector.
Some of concrete examples of GT' achievements include:
- GT in Stip grew from a volunteer based activist group into a well-established organisation recognized as a relevant stakeholder in the textile sector by workers, companies as well as local and national government as a promotor of social dialogue.
- GT's work on increasing visibility around the issue of textile workers' working conditions led to a drastic increase in complaints regarding violations of workers' rights, which contributed to increased efficiency and transparency in the country's labor inspectorate.
- GT together with another partner organization, SIER, actively advocated for workers' rights during the drafting process of the new labour law based on a close monitoring of the reform process. They were also part of the negotiations with the government on the level of minimum wages.
There was also continouos work and focus on increasing awareness with the yearly Textilijada festival in Stip organized by GT, which has become a meeting point for all actors in the textile industry to discuss the sustainability of the sector. GT has built various coalitions and partnerships, including with local government, public enterprises, universities and other CSOs.
GT has developed a close relation with the Swedish trade union Handels based on exchange and study visits to learn from each other and promote a closer cooperation with the European trade union movement. GT also organized a study visit to the city of Borås to take part of the transformation of the Swedish textile industry together with representatives from companies and the local and national government, with the idea of knowledge exchange and bringing lessons of the Swedish transition of the textile city of Borås to the textile city of Stip.
OPC also states that GT has also gained the recognition of public institutions and was contacted by the Public Revenue Administration to learn more about the cases handled by the association and how the PRA can help fight corruption cases involving companies in the textile sector. GT regularly participated in meetings with both the local and national government and has established a formal cooperation with the Labour Inspectorate and the Public Revenue Office.
As women make up 90% of the textile industry's employees, GT work with special attention to womens rights and issues such as gender discrimination and unequal salaries.
2. Trade Union of Industry, Energy and Mining (SIER) - OPC initially focused on support to structural reform strengthening internal democracy and the participation of members in decision-making processes.
Some examples of the most notable achievements of SIER are:
- Since the start of the collaboration SIER made significant progress and increased its membership by 150% (from 4 000 to 10 000 members) and succeeded in organising workers inside economic free zones which had not happened earlier.
- SIER was asked by the Ministry of Labour and Social Policy, and participated in the process of drafting the new labour law.
- SIER created a Womens section through the support of the Swedish union IF Metall as part of the modernizing of its structures and increased its presence in different workplaces offering trainings for union representatives.
SIER has also initiated work to raise awareness on the issue among members and to promote a socially Just Transition. Also, in this work SIER collaborated with Swedish IF Metall and the IndustriALL federation representing workers in the mining, energy, and manufacturing sectors in Europe.
3. Foundation for Debate and Education IDEA - During the programme period, IDEA partnered with OPC in a project focused on bringing together all OPC partners in North Macedonia to promote and profile their experiences utilizing multimedia platforms.
Some concrete examples of their work are:
- IDEA contributed to the public debate by producing several video stories on workers rights, where the personal stories of workers whose rights were not respected were showcased, which led to an increased participation and awareness.
- Through its social media and multimedia channels, IDEA reached in total over 1 million viewers during 2022, compared to the set goal of 700 000. Special attention was given to the socio-economic topics and stories of violations of workers rights.
4. NGO Info-Centar - During 2020-2022, NGO Info-Centar partnered with OPC and focused on the increased participation of citizens in decision-making processes.
Concrete examples of their work include:
- The cooperation with OPC grew from an individual project with NGO Info-Centar to a wider network with five small CSOs in Spektar, Norgesvel, Kriva Palanka, Negotino and Veles aimed at increasing participation and influence in decision-making processes.
- NGO Info-Centar as reported in the final programme report, has successfully expanded its network of local CSOs to cover more municipalities and built the foundation for a more structured cooperation between the participating organisations.
- Before the municipal elections in 2021, NGO Info-Centar formed the coalition Forum for Civil Dialogue (FCD) involving organisations in nine municipalities to channel citizens priorities to the political parties and to organize debates with the candidates and the local community. The coalition continues to monitor the work of the elected mayors.
The FCD, led by NGO InfoCentar, developed into a solid platform for building new alliances guiding citizens to make their voices heard in decisionmaking processes. The coalition also focused on building internal capacities making it eligible for additional donor support to sustain and further increase its influence
5. Youth Cultural Center, Bitola (MKC Bitola) - Some of the most notable work of MKC Bitola is that:
- MKC was instrumental in activating and improving the functionality of Local Economic-Social Councils (LESCs). OPC has since 2020 supported MKC to promote the Local Economic-Social Councils (LESCs) in eight municipalities as part of North Macedonias commitment to strengthen social dialogue.
The project initially focused on activating LESCs by establishing procedures and protocols for the work of the Councils based on International Labour Organization (ILO) recommendations for tripartite consultative bodies. The project then worked with the participating actors companies, trade unions and local government on specific actions plans for each municipality and the work has gained recognition in the communities as a promoter of economic and social development. Furthermore, the project enabled MKC to establish partnerships with similar institutions in Croatia, bringing EU experience closer to North Macedonia.
The final programme report states that the increased number of citizens and government institutions using MKC Bitola services demonstrates the organisation's legitimacy. It goes on to state that the work on activating Local Economic-Social Councils have involved the municipal governments and labour market stakeholders and they all recognize MKCs catalytic role in the work.
